subject: Post-call: cost guardrails & batching/caching pilot — next steps
messages:
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@finq-payments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-21T09:12:00Z
Subject: Post-call: cost guardrails & batching/caching pilot — next steps

Hi Elena — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap while it’s fresh and a proposed set of next steps so we can unblock a cost-focused pilot.

Summary of pain points you shared:
- Peak inference spend hits your monthly budget cap in high-volume auth windows (early morning PST).
- Latency SLO (95th <= 250ms) is critical for fraud check flows — you can’t trade more than ~20ms for cost savings.
- Visibility gap: you don’t currently have per-route token telemetry tied to customer segments, so it’s hard to prioritize where to optimize.

Goals we agreed on:
1) Validate a 6–8 week pilot that proves a 20–30% unit-cost reduction while keeping 95p latency within 250ms.
2) Show expected ROI for production rollout (C-suite ask: expected payback within 6 months).
3) Deliver a short ops playbook (batching + prefix/KV caching + light quantization) that your infra team can operate.

Initial technical levers we recommend exploring during pilot:
- Continuous micro-batching for low-latency steady state requests (adaptive batch sizes up to 8 tokens/batch).
- Request-level prefix caching for repeated invoice/merchant prompts (we estimate ~12–18% token-level reduction on conserved prefixes).
- Low-impact quantization on model checkpoints (int8 where possible) to lower GPU unit cost while measuring quality drift on key prompt set.

Quick cost math (rough ballpark we discussed):
- Baseline: ~3.8M tokens/day across auth+enrichment routes -> ~$5.2k/day at current throughput profile.
- Target: 20% reduction -> saves ~$1.0k/day (~$30k/month).

Proposed next steps (actions & owners):
1) FinQ: share a 2-week sample of request traces and 1 representative prompt set (sensitive fields redacted) — Elena (you)
2) Redwood: run a 10-day baseline run in our sandbox to measure per-route token counts and p95 latency with no optimizations — Ben
3) Redwood: run comparative run with batching + prefix caching + quantization flags and produce a side-by-side cost/latency/quality report — Ben & Lukas
4) Marissa: prepare an explicit pilot SOW and high-level pricing/commit options tied to observed savings — Marissa

Attachments: pilot-scope-finq.xlsx (pilot milestones), sample-traces-20261118.jsonl (please redact PII before sending back), redwood-pilot-sow-draft.pdf (initial SOW template).

Can you confirm: 1) ability to share traces by EOD Thursday (2026-11-25)? 2) any procurement gating items we should loop in now?

Thanks — happy to jump on a 15m follow-up if that helps.

— Lukas
Lukas Meyer

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-21T17:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call: cost guardrails & batching/caching pilot — next steps

Lukas / Marissa — quick technical note to help set expectations for FinQ around batching/caching tradeoffs: 

- Adaptive micro-batching: when traffic is steady we can batch up to N=8 with sub-ms enqueueing; p95 impact is typically +10–25ms depending on sequence length distributions. For short auth prompts (avg 30 tokens) expect ~+12–18ms.
- Prefix/KV caching: this is managed by Redwood when you run via Dedicated or Hosted with a cache policy. FinQ will not need to operate a separate cache service; we do need example prompts to identify common prefixes. Effective saving depends on prefix reuse; for commerce auth flows we often see 8–20% token savings.
- Quantization: int8 can reduce GPU cost by ~30% but we’ll run quality regressions on FinQ’s key prompt set. Typically we can keep semantic quality high for classification-like checks (fraud / risk heuristics).

I’ll include a short experiment plan in the sandbox run — baseline (no opts), batching-only, caching-only, batching+caching, and batching+caching+quant. Each run = 48–72 hours to stabilize metrics.

Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
